import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_8.csv", index_col=0)
source9 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/training_9.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename columns in source1 to match join keys for clarity
# source1 has 'sampled_bid_id' which corresponds to 'bid_id' in other sources
# We'll join on source1.sampled_bid_id = source0.bid_id

# First join source1 and source0 on sampled_bid_id = bid_id
df = pd.merge(
    source1,
    source0,
    left_on="sampled_bid_id",
    right_on="bid_id",
    how="inner",
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Join the rest of the sources one by one on 'bid_id'
# All other sources have 'bid_id' column
for src in [source2, source3, source4, source5, source6, source7, source8, source9]:
    df = pd.merge(
        df,
        src,
        on="bid_id",
        how="inner",
        suffixes=('', '_dup')
    )
    # Remove duplicated columns created by suffixes except the first occurrence
    dup_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.endswith('_dup')]
    df.drop(columns=dup_cols, inplace=True)

# The target schema has many columns with suffixes and duplicates due to multiple joins.
# The join keys and columns are preserved as is, no renaming or assignment to columns.

# GroupBy on all columns except aggregation (no aggregation needed as per hints)
# The leftmost columns in target schema are bid_id (int), message_timestamp (string), message_sender_x (string), message (string), category_x (string), agent_group (string), bid_id_header_x (float)
# But since the target schema is wide with many columns, and no aggregation is specified, group by all columns to remove duplicates if any.

# Group by all columns to remove duplicates (no aggregation)
df = df.groupby(list(df.columns)).size().reset_index().drop(columns=0)

# Write output to the specified path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_70/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
